title: Quasi-equivalence invariance of derived dg functor categories
statement:
Use universes large enough for the categories and complexes below [def-weil-size-convention]. A dg category over $\mathbf Z$ has a set of objects, cochain complexes of morphisms with degree-$1$ square-zero differentials, and unital associative chain-map compositions. A dg functor $u:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ is a quasi-equivalence if it induces maps on every morphism complex that are quasi-isomorphisms (isomorphisms on every cohomology group) and $H^0u$ is essentially surjective; $H^0$ takes degree-zero cohomology of every morphism complex. Let $\mathsf{Hqe}$ be the localization of small dg categories at these quasi-equivalences, and let $\mathsf{dgCat}_{\mathrm{qe}}$ denote the enhanced localization, which also retains homotopies between dg functors.

This dg homotopy theory admits derived tensor products and derived dg functor categories $\mathbf R\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{dg}}(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)$, with homotopy coherent composition and transformation complexes. On $\mathsf{Hqe}$ the latter is the internal Hom for derived tensor product. One model is the full dg subcategory of homotopically projective $\mathcal J_c$-$\mathcal B$ bimodules $T$, that is dg functors $\mathcal J_c\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ch}(\mathbf Z)$, for which every right $\mathcal B$-module $T(j,-)$ is objectwise quasi-isomorphic to $\mathcal B(-,b_j)$ for some $b_j$. The complex of bimodule maps consists of homogeneous graded bimodule maps with differential $df=d_{T'}f-(-1)^{|f|}f d_T$; objectwise acyclic means that each value has zero cohomology in every degree. Homotopically projective means that this complex of maps into every objectwise acyclic bimodule is acyclic. Here a dg category $\mathcal D$ is cofibrant if every dg functor from $\mathcal D$ lifts across every dg functor $\mathcal C_1\to\mathcal C_2$ which is surjective on objects and degreewise a surjective quasi-isomorphism on every morphism complex. A cofibrant replacement $\mathcal J_c\to\mathcal J$ is a quasi-equivalence with cofibrant source. Such replacements exist; their morphism complexes are homotopically flat over $\mathbf Z$, meaning tensoring them preserves quasi-isomorphisms. The bimodule Hom complexes compute derived natural transformations, not underived equalizers of component maps. Equivalently, a quasi-functor may be represented by a dg functor after a cofibrant replacement of its source, with transformations taken in the derived dg functor category.

Derived precomposition and postcomposition with a quasi-equivalence induce enhanced equivalences of these derived dg functor categories. In particular for every small dg category $\mathcal J$ and every quasi-equivalence $u:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ the induced map
$$u_*:\mathbf R\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{dg}}(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)\longrightarrow\mathbf R\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathrm{dg}}(\mathcal J,\mathcal C)$$
is an equivalence, including quasi-isomorphisms of transformation complexes, and an equivalence on the spaces of objects and invertible coherent transformations. The space here is the maximal homotopy groupoid of the enhanced category: it includes all higher homotopies between invertible transformations. These constructions are natural in $\mathcal J$ and compatible with composition and identities. The analogous assertion holds contravariantly in $\mathcal J$; no flatness assumption is imposed on the original dg categories.

proof.text: Choose the functorial replacements $Q\mathcal A\to\mathcal A$ of [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. Its trivial fibrations are exactly the maps used in the statement's lifting definition, so these are replacements in precisely that sense. Their morphism complexes are homotopically flat. Set $\mathcal A\otimes^L\mathcal B=Q\mathcal A\otimes Q\mathcal B$. To see independence under quasi-equivalences, factor the tensor of two maps on any morphism complex into tensoring in one variable and then the other; the unchanged factor is homotopically flat in each case. Essential surjectivity follows by taking pairs of representatives of the two target objects; the tensor of two invertible $H^0$ arrows remains invertible. Thus the tensor of quasi-equivalences between these flat models is a quasi-equivalence. Also $Q\mathcal J\otimes Q\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}\to Q\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$ is a quasi-equivalence, by flatness of $Q\mathcal J$. Under [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification] these tensor products give the tensor of the derived enrichments: their mapping objects are the derived tensors of the two mapping complexes. The coherent associativity, symmetry and units are therefore those of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus], applied to $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$. This constructs the derived tensor with no flatness condition on the original inputs.

source.place: Sections 2 and 4, Proposition 2.3 and the derived tensor preceding Definition 4.1; derived-enrichment comparison.

proof.text: For $\mathcal D=Q\mathcal J\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$, take the full dg category $\mathcal R(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)$ of homotopically projective covariant $\mathcal D$-modules whose fibers are quasi-representable right $\mathcal B$-modules. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-projective-resolution] to $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$; covariant $\mathcal D$-modules are right $\mathcal D^{\mathrm{op}}$-modules. It supplies homotopically projective replacements and identifies their actual Hom complexes with derived mapping complexes. The fiber condition is unchanged by any objectwise quasi-isomorphism. The replacement of any module in this fiber class stays in the class. The cited statement therefore restricts to a presentation of this full enhanced subcategory: it is essentially surjective by these replacements and fully faithful by its derived-Hom assertion. An objectwise quasi-isomorphism between two of these homotopically projective modules is a chain homotopy equivalence by the same cited statement. In particular its Hom differential is exactly $df=d_{T'}f-(-1)^{|f|}fd_T$, and these complexes carry all derived module transformations. The full subcategory can be taken in a larger universe as stipulated in [def-weil-size-convention].

source.place: Section 3, projective modules and projective model structure; Section 6, the model Int of right quasi-representable bimodules.

proof.text:
Let $\mathcal A$ be a cofibrant test dg category. By [lem-coef-dgcat-bimodule-mapping-space], morphisms $\mathcal A\otimes^L\mathcal J\to\mathcal B$ in $\mathsf{Hqe}$ classify right quasi-representable modules over $(\mathcal A\otimes Q\mathcal J)\otimes\mathcal B^{\mathrm{op}}$. The independence shown in step 1 permits using the already cofibrant $\mathcal A$ in the derived tensor; $\mathcal A\otimes Q\mathcal J$ is flat even though it need not be cofibrant, so its further cofibrant replacement gives the same classification. Explicit currying identifies such a module $T$ with the strict $\mathcal A$-diagram $a\mapsto T(a,-,-)$ of $\mathcal D$-modules: both data have the same values and the same commuting actions, and maps, differentials and objectwise quasi-isomorphisms are unchanged. The quasi-representable condition says precisely that every value of this diagram has quasi-representable $\mathcal B$-fibers. This class $\mathcal S$ of $\mathcal D$-modules is closed under quasi-isomorphisms in both directions. Apply [lem-coef-dg-module-diagram-classification] with this $\mathcal D$, $\mathcal S$ and cofibrant $\mathcal A$. It gives, naturally in the test category,
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal A\otimes^L\mathcal J,\mathcal B)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathsf{Hqe}}(\mathcal A,\mathcal R(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)).$$
For an arbitrary test category replace it cofibrantly using [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure]. This proves the internal-Hom universal property on $\mathsf{Hqe}$ by an argument with module diagrams, rather than by invoking the internal-Hom theorem itself.

source.place: Section 6, proof of Theorem 6.1: the two displayed classifications using Corollary 4.8 and Lemma 6.2.

proof.text: Use $\mathcal U$-small module values in step 2. By [lem-coef-dgfunctor-small-model], the projective quasi-representable model $\mathcal R$ has a $\mathcal U$-small full dg subcategory $\mathcal R_0$ representing every $H^0$-isomorphism class. Its inclusion is a quasi-equivalence. Thus the representing object of step 3 can be taken in the same small universe as the coherent enriched internal Hom.

source.place: Corollary 4.11, including its proof of essential smallness.

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-dgfunctor-rectified-model-comparison] to $\mathcal R_0$. Step 1 supplies compatibility of the derived and enriched tensors, and step 3 supplies its natural representing bijections; the quasi-equivalence of step 4 preserves them. The comparison gives an equivalence from $\mathcal R_0$ to a rectification of $\mathcal F=\operatorname{Fun}_{\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)}(\mathcal J,\mathcal B)$, respecting evaluation. It identifies mapping objects with those of $\mathcal R_0$, hence with the projective-bimodule Hom complexes computed in step 2.

source.place: Haugseng, Rectification of enriched infinity-categories, Theorem 5.8 and Example 5.11; representing-object comparison combined with the closed tensor in On the tensor product of enriched infinity-categories, Remark 9.5 (https://arxiv.org/html/2311.13362v1). Agent specialization; read online, not archived. No Stacks tag supplies this dg-enriched comparison.

proof.text: Choose these equivalences for the pairs of dg categories under consideration. Apply [lem-coef-dgfunctor-coherent-transport] to transport the coherent internal-Hom evaluation, composition and identity structures to their projective-bimodule models. Its comparison of two such families supplies all higher compatibility homotopies and identifies their derived transformation objects. This proves the required independence of model choices at the enhanced level.

source.place: Remark 9.5 and Corollary 10.8, specialized to coherent enriched functor categories.

proof.text: A quasi-equivalence $u:\mathcal B\to\mathcal C$ becomes an equivalence of derived enriched categories by [lem-coef-dg-enrichment-rectification]. Choose its inverse $v$, with coherent unit and counit. Postcomposition gives $u_*$ and $v_*$ on the enriched functor categories of [lem-coef-enriched-category-tensor-calculus]. Whiskering the unit and counit gives $v_*u_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$ and $u_*v_*\simeq\mathrm{id}$, with their triangle homotopies. Hence $u_*$ is an enhanced equivalence. In particular it is fully faithful on mapping objects in $\mathbf D(\mathbf Z)$; using the model of steps 2-6, this is exactly quasi-isomorphism of the complexes of derived transformations. For a quasi-equivalence $w:\mathcal J'\to\mathcal J$, precomposition with an inverse of $w$ gives the inverse to $w^*$. The same whiskering of its unit and counit proves the contravariant assertion. Coherent composition, identity and naturality in all variables are inherited from the enriched functor operations of the cited tensor-calculus node.

source.place: Formal inverse-whiskering argument in the coherent enriched functor categories of tensor-calculus Remark 9.5.

proof.text: Restrict an enhanced equivalence and its inverse from step 7 to objects and invertible transformations. The same unit and counit remain inverse homotopies, so the maximal homotopy groupoids are equivalent, with every higher homotopy retained. Finally any object represented by a right quasi-representable bimodule gives a morphism $\mathcal J\to\mathcal B$ in $\mathsf{Hqe}$ by [lem-coef-dgcat-bimodule-mapping-space]. By [lem-coef-dgcat-model-structure] that morphism is represented by an actual dg functor $Q\mathcal J\to\mathcal B$, since its source is cofibrant and its target fibrant. The mapping-space classification identifies this representative with the original quasi-functor. Its transformations are still the derived ones computed in steps 2-6; this argument makes no assertion that strict equalizers of transformations have become homotopy invariant.

source.place: Section 2, cofibrant-to-fibrant representatives; Section 4, Corollary 4.8; maximal homotopy groupoids of the equivalence in step 7.
